attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

def concatenate_benchmarks(data, exposure_scores, benchmarks=None,
                           exclude_rules=None, max_items=None, seed=42):
    """Concatenate all benchmark data into a single response/exposure matrix.

    Args:
        data: output of load_eval_results
        exposure_scores: per-benchmark tau vectors
        benchmarks: subset of benchmarks to include (None=all)
        exclude_rules: list of dicts {"model", "benchmark", "reason"}.
            When a model matching the pattern is present, that benchmark
            is excluded from the joint fit.

    Returns:
        dict with y, exposure, dosages, benchmark_slices, valid_models
    """
    dosages = data["dosages"]
    models = data["models"]
    bench_names = benchmarks or list(data["benchmarks"].keys())

    excluded_benchmarks = set()
    if exclude_rules:
        model_names = [m["model_name"] for m in models]
        for rule in exclude_rules:
            rule_model = rule.get("model", "")
            rule_bench = rule.get("benchmark", "")
            if any(rule_model in mn for mn in model_names):
                excluded_benchmarks.add(rule_bench.lower())
                log.info("Exclude rule: skipping benchmark %s (model=%s, reason=%s)",
                         rule_bench, rule_model, rule.get("reason", "n/a"))

    all_y = []
    all_exposure = []
    slices = {}
    col_offset = 0

    for bench in bench_names:
        if bench not in data["benchmarks"]:
            continue

            continue

        responses = bd["responses"]
        valid = bd["valid_mask"]
        tau = exposure_scores[bench]
        n_items = bd["n_items"]

            dosages_valid = dosages[valid]
        else:

            dosages_valid = dosages

        if max_items and n_items > max_items:

            idx = np.sort(rng.choice(n_items, max_items, replace=False))

    """Fit a single IRT model with shared gamma across all benchmarks."""
    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if pool_scales:
        data = load_pooled_eval_results(eval_dir, pool_scales, benchmarks,
                                         seed_filter=seed_filter,
                                         aligned_only=aligned_only)
    else:

                                  model_scale=model_scale,
                                  seed_filter=seed_filter,
                                  aligned_only=aligned_only)

    concat = concatenate_benchmarks(data, exposure_scores, benchmarks,

                                    max_items=max_items, seed=seed)

    exposure = concat["exposure"]
    log.info("Joint fit: %d models x %d total items", y.shape[0], y.shape[1])

    stan_data = prepare_stan_data(y, exposure)

    fit, elapsed = fit_stan_model(

        chains=chains, iter_warmup=warmup, iter_sampling=samples,

    ppc = posterior_predictive_check(fit, y)

exp-006 end-to-end pipeline: IRT calibration + 7 baselines + evaluation.

Loads exp-001 eval results and exp-002/003 exposure scores,
runs IRT 4PL+gamma calibration and all baselines per benchmark,

)

# D018: 3B GSM8K excluded from dose-response analysis

]


def should_exclude_dose_response(model_name, benchmark, rules=D018_EXCLUDE):
    """Check D018 exclusion rules for dose-response analysis."""
    for pattern, bench in rules:
        if pattern in model_name and benchmark == bench:
            return True
    return False


def compute_ground_truth(responses, dosages, models=None):
    """Ground truth = accuracy of dosage-0 models (uncontaminated).

    For dosage-0 models, raw accuracy IS the clean accuracy.
    For dosage>0 models, we use the mean d=0 accuracy of the SAME SCALE
    as the counterfactual reference.
    """
    raw_acc = responses.mean(axis=1)
    d0_mask = dosages == 0

    # Global d0 mean as fallback
    if d0_mask.sum() > 0:
        global_d0_mean = float(raw_acc[d0_mask].mean())
    else:
        global_d0_mean = float(raw_acc.mean())

    # Per-scale counterfactual when models have scale info
    scales = None
    if models is not None:
        scales = [m.get("scale", "") for m in models]
    has_multiscale = scales and len(set(s for s in scales if s)) > 1

    if has_multiscale:
        ground_truth = np.empty(len(dosages))
        for i, (d, sc) in enumerate(zip(dosages, scales)):
            if d == 0:
                ground_truth[i] = raw_acc[i]
            else:
                same_scale_d0 = [
                    j for j in range(len(dosages))
                    if dosages[j] == 0 and scales[j] == sc
                ]
                if same_scale_d0:
                    ground_truth[i] = float(raw_acc[same_scale_d0].mean())
                else:
                    log.warning("No d0 models for scale %s, using global mean", sc)
                    ground_truth[i] = global_d0_mean
        unique_scales = sorted(set(scales))
        for sc in unique_scales:
            sc_d0 = [j for j in range(len(dosages)) if dosages[j] == 0 and scales[j] == sc]
            if sc_d0:
                log.info("Ground truth [%s]: d0 mean=%.4f (n=%d)",
                         sc, float(raw_acc[sc_d0].mean()), len(sc_d0))
    else:
        ground_truth = np.full(len(dosages), global_d0_mean)
        ground_truth[d0_mask] = raw_acc[d0_mask]

    return ground_truth


def load_exp002_signals(signals_dir, models, benchmark, signal_key=None,
                        pool_mode=False):
    """Load exp-002 merged signals -> per-model contamination score.
    D023/D030: 3-signal RRF fusion (S1+S2+S4), S2 polarity flipped.
    """
    scores = []
    for m in models:
        # Strip _aligned/_para suffixes to match signal directory naming
        sig_dirname = m["dirname"].replace("_para_aligned", "").replace("_aligned", "").replace("_para", "")
        merged = os.path.join(signals_dir, sig_dirname,
                              "signals_merged_{}.json".format(benchmark))
        if os.path.exists(merged):
            with open(merged) as f:
                items = json.load(f)
            n = len(items)
            rrf = np.zeros(n)
            for sig in ("s1_embedding", "s2_minkpp", "s4_selfcritique"):
                v = np.array([it.get(sig, 0.0) or 0.0 for it in items])
                if sig == "s2_minkpp":
                    v = -v
                order = np.argsort(-v)
                ranks = np.empty(n)
                ranks[order] = np.arange(1, n + 1)
                rrf += 1.0 / (60 + ranks)
            mn, mx = rrf.min(), rrf.max()

        else:

                    f"Signal homogeneity violation: no signals for "
                    f"{m['dirname']}/{benchmark} in pooled mode. "
                    f"Cannot mix signal-derived and oracle exposure.")
            log.warning("No exp-002 signals for %s/%s, falling back to oracle dosage",

            scores.append(m["dosage"] / 100.0)

    excluded = set()

            for bench in benchmarks:

                    break
